A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
R5X4 is a phenotype associated to gp41 with a tendency to have a more hydrophobic HR2, and a more hydrophilic/ionic C-terminal tail.
R5X4 phenotype may arise from the accumulation of amino acids with hydrophobic properties in gp41, which could be a consequence of an adaptive process to escape immune pressure.

the gp41 variable amino acids have a significant role in viral phenotype, and that these residues are potential targets for the design of drugs and vaccines.
